title: Short Stuff: Robert the Doll
summary: Short Stuff episode on Robert the Doll, the antique cork-faced doll said to be the lifelong companion of Robert Eugene "Gene" Otto of Key West, Florida. The hosts cover the doll's origins (a gift from Gene's grandfather, possibly made by the Steiff company), the mischief legends blamed on Robert, Gene's adult life in the Artist House with his wife Anne Parker, the attic room, the house sale to Myrtle Reuter with the condition that Robert stay, the doll's move to the East Martello Museum, the belief that photographing him without permission brings bad luck, and the low-budget Robert movies and sequels. Recorded as part of the Halloween-week creepy edition.

segments.title: Halloween intro and viewing Robert's photos
segments.summary: Josh introduces the Halloween Short Stuff and suggests listeners look up images of Robert the doll before listening, describing the creepy antique look and the modern movie version.

segments.title: Robert's origins and Gene's childhood
segments.summary: The hosts describe Robert as a three-foot straw-filled cork-faced doll given to Robert Eugene 'Gene' Otto by his grandfather after a trip to Germany, likely made by Steiff, possibly as a harlequin jester. Gene blamed Robert for his misdeeds, and family and workers reported unexplained sounds and movement.

segments.title: Gene's adult life, the Artist House and the attic room
segments.summary: Gene becomes a painter after studying in Chicago and Paris, marries Anne Parker, and keeps Robert with him in the Artist House on Eton Street. Accounts say Robert was kept in an attic room built for him, and that he was repeatedly found in a rocking chair by a bedroom window.

segments.title: Sale of the house, museum move, and photo permission legend
segments.summary: After Gene's death, Anne sold the house to Myrtle Reuter on the condition that Robert stay in the attic. Myrtle later took Robert and cared for him for about twenty years before donating him to the East Martello Museum in the mid-1990s. The hosts relate the belief that you must ask Robert's permission before photographing him, and a story of a camera that failed.

segments.title: Robert movies and sequels
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the low-budget Robert film and its four sequels, including Robert Reborn, noting they are loosely based on the story and compared unfavorably to Chucky.

segments.title: Credits and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts credit sources and a contributor, encourage listeners to visit Robert at the East Martello Museum, and sign off.
